derived.prompt: p is a prime number greater than 2. What is the remainder when p is divided by 2?

chain: p is a prime number greater than 2. (given in prompt)
Every prime number greater than 2 is even. (edit)

derived.prompt: A bag holds a prime number of marbles, and that number is greater than 2. If the marbles are shared equally between two children, is one marble left over?

derived.fact: A prime number of marbles greater than 2, shared equally between two children, leaves one marble over.
chain: The number of marbles is a prime number greater than 2. (given in prompt)
Every prime number greater than 2 is even. (edit)
So the number is even, and the marbles split equally with none left over.

Every prime number greater than 2 is odd.why: Stated directly on Wikipedia and, in its equivalent form '2 is the only even prime', thousands of times in Dolma.

sources.quote: Therefore, every prime number other than 2 is an odd number, and is called an odd prime.

sources.query: all primes greater than 2 are odd
prime number greater than 2 is odd

The newly discovered prime Q, which has.why: An unnamed new prime: its parity is never written down; the rule (or its equivalent, 2 is the only even prime) gives it.

sources.query: prime number with millions of digits

A prime number p greater than 2 leaves a.why: The remainder of an unnamed prime is worked out from its parity, which comes from the rule.

p divided by 2 leaves a remainder of 1

sources.note: The usual way proofs introduce an odd prime: an assumption about p, not the remainder asked here.

A prime number of marbles greater than 2.why: A word problem no text contains: the parity of the count comes from the rule, and an even count splits evenly.

A right angle measures 90 degrees..why: The definition of a right angle, the first sentence of its Wikipedia article.

sources.quote: In geometry and trigonometry, a right angle is an angle of exactly 90 degrees or π/2 radians corresponding to a quarter turn.

9 is a prime number..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited rule: 9 = 3 × 3 is composite.

sources.quote: 9 is the fourth composite number, the first odd composite number, a square, a Motzkin number, and the number of derangements of 4 items.

notes: TBox rule, stored (very_unlikely; was 'unlikely', no longer a value): Wikipedia states it and its equivalent '2 is the only even prime' is stated thousands of times. Mathematics TBox revision: the three derived queries apply the edited rule to new members named in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops: the edit plus the membership the prompt states), so no stored fact about a well-known member (a named number or figure) offers a route back to the old answer, and every answer is determinate. The earlier well-known-member queries were dropped for that reason. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the propositional side facts need checks. New members: an unnamed newly discovered prime Q with millions of digits, an unnamed prime p (remainder mod 2) and a prime number of marbles (an application: split between two children). The old well-known-member queries (7; 3 × 5) were dropped: their answers are reachable by direct computation, and the check "3 and 5 are prime numbers greater than 2" was missed by two models in its yes/no form. A model could still reason that any prime above 2 is odd because it is not divisible by 2; that is the rule itself, so it is what the edit has to overturn. The disjunction now uses a false side fact (9 is prime). The near query (is 2 prime?) shares the subject class and does not follow from the edit, which is about primes above 2; its answer differs from the new answer (Rule 7). Relation has_parity (functional: a whole number is odd or even, not both).
